newsitem.title: HUNGARY: HOT WEATHER MOVES HUNGARY GRAIN PRICES.
newsitem.headline: HOT WEATHER MOVES HUNGARY GRAIN PRICES.

text.p: Hungary's milling wheat futures closed mixed on Tuesday but rose for the most liquid maturities on a forecast of unseasonally hot weather for the rest of this week, traders said.

Grains futures turnover on the Budapest Commodity Exchange (BCE) rose to a modest 328 million forints from a meagre 102.6 million on Monday, but traders said that despite higher turnover speculation was still the main mover of prices.
Milling wheat futures accounted for 426 of the total 738 lots traded in the BCE grain section, most of which was for July and August.
July milling wheat rose a limit-up 400 forints to 23,900 while August rose 150 forints to 24,100.
July maize also saw heavy turnover, seeing a limit-up rise to 19,300 forints.

Anticipation of improved future harvests as a result of the current heat wave brought longer term maturities down, with December milling wheat and next March milling wheat maize falling a limit-down 400 to 26,100, 27,100 and 21,400 respectively.
Trade in other grains was minimal.
